sam_support: Heads-up — ACME emailed in with a regression: identical rerank payloads are returning different rank orders after last night's runtime merge. No HTTP errors (200s). Same request body, different score arrays + top-1 flips. Example below.

emily_cs: Customer says it started ~2027-03-02 02:10 UTC after a deploy. They provided two POSTs that are byte-for-byte identical but got different top results.

sam_support: Minimal repro we received: 
```
POST /v1/rerank HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwoodinference.com
Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>
Content-Type: application/json

{"query":"best wireless earbuds","candidates":[{"id":"123","text":"Foo Earbuds"},{"id":"456","text":"Bar Pods"},{"id":"789","text":"Baz Audio"}]}
```
Customer sent it twice within seconds. Response A top id=123, scores=[0.72,0.44,0.22]. Response B top id=789, scores=[0.41,0.36,0.68]. Both 200, different ranking. Request IDs: req-acme-01, req-acme-02.

deploy-bot: Deployed commit abc123 to inference-runtime-prod at 2027-03-02T02:05:12Z (rollout 10%).

raj_engineering: Noted. Two immediate possibilities: nondeterministic kernel behavior (fp16/math reductions) or a race in post-processing (normalization / softmax step) when batching/caching paths diverge. Do we have model/version + quant profile? Any seed/deterministic flag set?

sam_support: Model: redwood-rerank-v3.1 (customer had model pinned). Quant profile: mixed-int8-fp16. No explicit seed set from client. Batch size observed: sometimes 2-8 depending on traffic. Will attach raw payloads and request-level headers.

jordan_infra: Rollout target pool A (gpu-nodegroup-b) got the new runtime. We can pause rollouts. If engineering wants rollback we can do it immediately.

sam_support: Customer captured traces and attached tokenized output — tokens identical between the two requests. They included two server traces with headers X-Trace: trace-331 and trace-332.

raj_engineering: Can reproduce locally with mixed quant on a small sample — I see tiny fp16 nondeterminism but not flips that large. However, when batch path uses cached KV + streaming merge I can force a normalization that reads a shared buffer concurrently. Suspect a race in logits->score normalization when concurrent batches hit the same normalization buffer.

emily_cs: I'll tell the customer we're actively investigating and ask for permission to run their test payloads against a canary with extra logging.

sam_support: Customer ok'd it and ran two more hits against a canary endpoint. Results show same flip. Attaching trace IDs and raw score dumps from their runs (sanitized).

raj_engineering: Plan: 1) force per-request normalization (avoid shared buffer) + add a unit test that replays identical requests 1000x and asserts deterministic ranks; 2) deploy small patch to canary (no model changes). If stable, roll forward; if not, rollback abc123.

deploy-bot: Canary patch abc124 deployed to inference-runtime-prod-canary at 2027-03-02T03:10:05Z.

raj_engineering: Early canary results look promising — ran 200 identical pairs, 0 flips so far. Need more samples and customer verification.

sam_support: Running a 500-pair sweep now through the canary and will post aggregated stats in this thread. Marking P1 and linking ticket INC-4579.

emily_cs: Thanks all. I'll keep ACME updated with ETA for full rollback if needed. :pray:

sam_support: Summary to add to ticket: identical payloads -> different rank orders after runtime merge abc123; no 5xx; tokenization identical; suspected race in normalization buffer with mixed quant/batched path; patch abc124 to force per-request normalization deployed to canary; running extended repro sweep.

jordan_infra: Keeping rollback ready; standby for final decision.
